sentences.text:
Apprehending their arrest, petitioners above-named have moved this Court for
grant of anticipatory bail in connection with Ormanjhi P.S. Case No.163 of 2021 registered under
Sections 406, 420, 467, 468, 471, 34 of the Indian Penal Code.
sentences._hearing_file: Santosh Kumar vs The State Of Jharkhand on 18 August, 2023.json

sentences.text: Heard the parties.
sentences._hearing_file: Santosh Kumar vs The State Of Jharkhand on 18 August, 2023.json

sentences.text:
It is submitted by learned counsel for the petitioners that the alleged offence under Sections 406 &
420 IPC will not be made out as against them as the Sale deed was executed by the petitioner(s) on the strength of power of attorney executed by accused no.1 to 6 who happens to be the joint family members of the informant/complainant.
sentences._hearing_file: Santosh Kumar vs The State Of Jharkhand on 18 August, 2023.json

sentences.text: There was no intention to deceive as under the bona-fide belief the sale-deed(s) was executed.
sentences._hearing_file: Santosh Kumar vs The State Of Jharkhand on 18 August, 2023.json

sentences.text: The main grievance of the complainant/ informant is that without proper partition the share has been disposed of by accused no.1 to 6.
sentences._hearing_file: Santosh Kumar vs The State Of Jharkhand on 18 August, 2023.json

sentences.text: The dispute between the parties is civil in nature.
sentences._hearing_file: Santosh Kumar vs The State Of Jharkhand on 18 August, 2023.json

sentences.text: Learned APP for the State has vehemently opposed the prayer.
sentences._hearing_file: Santosh Kumar vs The State Of Jharkhand on 18 August, 2023.json

sentences.text: Considering the submissions of learned counsel and the fact as discussed above, the anticipatory bail application is allowed.
sentences._hearing_file: Santosh Kumar vs The State Of Jharkhand on 18 August, 2023.json

sentences.text:
Hence,
in the event of their arrest or surrender within a period of three weeks from the date of receipt of a copy of this order before the learned court below, the petitioners named above shall be released on bail on furnishing bail bond of Rs.25,000/- (Rupees Twenty Five Thousand) each with two sureties of the like amount each to the satisfaction of learned Court below, subject to the conditions laid down under Section 438(2) Cr. P.C.
sentences._hearing_file: Santosh Kumar vs The State Of Jharkhand on 18 August, 2023.json

sentences.text:
The petitioners will co-operate in the investigation and will appear on notice under Section 41 A of Cr.P.C. as and when their presence is required and comply with the condition as laid down under Section 438(2) of the Cr.P.C.
(Gautam Kumar Choudhary, J.) Sandeep/uploaded.

04/ 04.12.2025 Petitioner Santosh Kumar has filed this writ application for quashing of the entire proceedings of Confiscation Case No. 07 of 2020-21 arising out of Ketar P.S. Case No. 48 of 2020 registered under sections 379/411/420/120/34 of the Indian Penal Code, Rule 54 of J.M.M.C (AR)
and section 21 of M.M.D.R Act in respect of confiscation of Poklane Machine which was seized and confiscated by the Informant party.
opennyai_summary.final__facts:
In the said confiscation proceeding, petitioner was directed to deposit Rs. 5.00 lakh as a condition for release of the vehicle.
It was submitted that Confiscation Case No. 07 of 2020-21 pending before the Deputy Commissioner-cum-District Magistrate, Garhwa is to be quashed as he is not the Confiscating Authority in terms of Jharkhand Minerals (Prevention of Illegal Mining, Transportation and Storage) Rules, 2017.
It was further submitted that the proceeding was initiated in terms of Rule 11(v) of Jharkhand Minerals (Prevention of Illegal Mining, Transportation and Storage) Rules, 2017, which has been declared ultra vires by the Division Bench of this Court vide order dated 22.04.2024 passed in W.P (C) No.

opennyai_summary.final__arguments:
Learned counsel for the State submits that since the vehicle has been released after deposit of Rs.
5.00 lakh, the same should not be returned to the petitioner.
opennyai_summary.final__decision:
4. Since the provision of law under which confiscation was done, has been declared ultra vires, the entire Confiscation Proceeding being Confiscation Case No. 07 of 2020-21 pending before the Deputy Commissioner-Cum- District Magistrate, Garhwa is set aside.
All consequential order is set aside.
The amount of Rs. 5.00 lakh deposited by the petitioner should be refunded to the petitioner within three weeks from the date of receipt of a copy of this order.
5. Accordingly, this writ application is allowed.
